title: Spintronic logic speed and switching energy
bottleneck: Spintronics (spin-transfer and spin-orbit torque devices) promise nonvolatile logic, but switching magnets is slower and more energy-hungry than charging CMOS gates at advanced nodes, and read/write asymmetry complicates circuit design. Scaling magnetic tunnel junctions below 10nm while retaining thermal stability fights fundamental superparamagnetic limits. Spintronic logic keeps losing the speed race to CMOS.
why_it_blocks: Nonvolatile logic could eliminate standby power and enable instant-on computing, but only if it matches CMOS speed. Until switching energy and delay improve by orders of magnitude, spintronics stays confined to memory (MRAM) rather than logic.
current_state: STT-MRAM is commercial as embedded memory, and spin-orbit-torque devices show faster switching in labs. Logic-grade speed and energy at scale remain unproven. Thermal stability requirements force larger magnetic volumes, which directly opposes the scaling needed for competitive density.
